thread:
maya (VP Eng): quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime segment — thanks for the great Qs. two things I want clarified asap: 1) batching+kv-cache rollout timeline for next quarter, and 2) who is the owner for the kernel v4 perf backlog?

sam (Runtime): timeline: feature-flagged start of canary next week, limited to dedicated clusters. broad rollout targeted mid-q (approx 6 weeks). final perf tuning after canary based on latency traces.

li (Eng-ML): kernel v4 perf backlog is mostly with our kernel team but we'll need help from model-ops for quantization testing. i'm volunteering to coordinate eval prompts.

maya (VP Eng): thanks li. sam — can you paste the canary scoping doc or link? also, what's the rollback plan if we see 2-5ms p95 regressions?

sam (Runtime): sure — doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/runtime/canary-v4 (internal). rollback plan: automatic fallback to v3 variant if p95 > baseline + 3ms for 10min window. manual override via console.

ben (Product): question: will caching changes be opt-in per-customer initially? we have enterprise customers asking for control.

sam (Runtime): yes — prefix/KV cache behavior will be configurable per-tenant. default is enabled for hosted, off for private unless explicitly enabled.

toni (SRE): based on today's talk, can we get a clear SLO impact matrix? i.e., if batching increases throughput but slightly worsens p95, what's acceptable for SRE?

maya (VP Eng): great point — i'll sync with SRE to define thresholds. short answer: latency SLOs remain; batching is tuned to respect latency budgets. if throughput gains require small p95 tradeoff it's allowed within defined guardrails (we'll publish numbers).

katie (Developer Experience): action item: can we publish a short 'what to expect' note for SDK users about streaming behavior changes during canary? small code refrain examples would help.

sam (Runtime): yes — i'll draft a short blurb and add code snippets. example snippet we'll include:

```
# python client: prefer streaming=True for low-latency tails
resp = client.generate(model="rwd-v4-kernel-canary", prompt="...")
for chunk in resp.stream():
    process(chunk)
```

li (Eng-ML): also adding: we'll run quality regressions using the eval set from /repos/inference-evals/kernel-v4. will post baseline metrics tomorrow.

ben (Product): depending on rollback sensitivity, customers may want opt-out toggles. flagging for enterprise success.

maya (VP Eng): agreed. ben, can you and sam define opt-out UX by EOD Friday? katie — will you help with docs?

ben (Product): yep, i'll draft UX copy. sam + katie — i'll loop you in.

sam (Runtime): noted. will create canary runbook and a one-click rollback play in the console.

deploy-bot: [deploy scheduled] canary rollout for rwd-v4-kernel starts 2025-06-03T10:00Z — target groups: dedicated-us-west, canary-1.

toni (SRE): heads up — i'll run chaos-check on the canary clusters 24hr pre-rollout to validate observability.

maya (VP Eng): awesome. final ask: who can be kernel-v4 single-threaded owner for day-to-day questions?

li (Eng-ML): i can be focal for model/quality; sam will be infra owner. li + sam = owners working with kernel team.

katie (Developer Experience): i'll prepare the FAQ and quickstart for SDKs. will ping when ready.

maya (VP Eng): perfect. action items recap: sam — canary runbook + rollback play; ben + sam + katie — opt-out UX + docs; li — eval baselines by tomorrow; toni — chaos-checks pre-rollout. i'll follow up in leadership sync on Friday. thanks all :raised_hands:

sam (Runtime): noted. i'll post the runbook link here when ready.

li (Eng-ML): baseline metrics will be in this thread when available.

katie (Developer Experience): draft docs ETA Thu EOD.

ben (Product): UX draft ETA Friday morning.

maya (VP Eng): if anyone wants to join the canary readiness call tmrw 11am PT ping me. :calendar:
